messages.content: You label student C submissions for a programming course. Reply with a JSON object only.

Task: a is sorted. Return 1 if two different cells add up to target, using two indexes that move inward; otherwise 0.
Signature: int pair_sum_exists(int a[], int n, int target)

Submission:
int pair_sum_exists(int a[],int n,int target){//two indexes move inward
int i=0,j=n-1,s;while(i<j){s=a[i]+a[j];if(s==target)return 1;if(s<target)i++;else j--;}
return 0;
//earlier attempt
/*
for(i=0;i<n;i++)for(j=i+1;j<n;j++)if(a[i]+a[j]==target)return 1;return 0;
*/
}

Choose exactly one label for this submission from the code alone:
- M01: Loop runs one step too many or too few. Wrong belief: `i<=n` (from 0) runs n times; whether the bound is the last value included or excluded is mixed up
- M02: Loop variable never moves toward the exit. Wrong belief: The loop variable advances by itself and the loop ends by itself
- M03: Running total is reset inside the loop. Wrong belief: The total keeps its value across passes even if it is set again inside the loop
- M04: int ÷ int drops the decimals. Wrong belief: int / int gives the exact decimal
- M05: Variable used before it was given a value. Wrong belief: Local variables start at 0
- M06: `=` stores a value; `==` compares. Wrong belief: `=` compares
- M07: A stray `;` gives the if/loop an empty body. Wrong belief: A `;` after the header is harmless
- M08: Arrays start at 0; last cell is n−1. Wrong belief: Arrays are indexed 1..n
- M10: `printf` shows a value; `return` hands it back. Wrong belief: Printing the value hands it back to the caller
- D01: The search gives up after the first miss. Wrong belief: The else branch means 'not this one, keep looking'; it doesn't end or overwrite anything
- D02: Binary search window never shrinks (`low = mid`). Wrong belief: mid is excluded from the window automatically
- D03: Swapping without a temp loses a value. Wrong belief: Two assignments happen at the same time
- D04: One pass doesn't sort the whole array. Wrong belief: One pass over the array sorts it
- D05: Recursion has no reachable base case. Wrong belief: Recursion stops by itself when the work is done
- D06: The recursive call doesn't move toward the base case. Wrong belief: The recursive call moves toward the base case on its own
- D07: The recursive call's result is thrown away. Wrong belief: The recursive call's result is combined automatically
- D08: `==` doesn't compare text in C. Wrong belief: `==` compares text
- CORRECT: it solves the task on every input.
- OTHER: it is wrong, but not because of any belief above.
- GATE: it is not a valid answer in the allowed C (wrong language, empty, hard-coded, uses pointers or scanf, no recursion where required).

Return JSON: {"label": "<one id from the list>"}
